behaviors.description: Remove an undeployed local ref while retaining its downloaded payload.
behaviors.preconditions: Independent deployed and second apps; HTTP server can deny content while continuing to serve metadata.
behaviors.expected: Removing deployed ref fails. Removing pulled-only ref prevents no-pull deployment, but a repull succeeds with content blocked and requests no payload; deployed commits remain intact.

behaviors.description: Observe orphaned payload deletion through controlled public repulls.
behaviors.preconditions: Deployed app and second app with independently required payload; public cleanup precedes pruning.
behaviors.expected: Cleanup removes the undeployed ref but retains repullable content. After another cleanup and prune, the same blocked-content repull fails and requests payload; restoring server access permits recovery with exact commits.

mappings.rationale: Deployed removal fails; pulled-only removal succeeds and invalidates no-pull deployment. A blocked-content repull then succeeds without payload requests, contrasting with its pre-download failure and establishing retained objects.

Identical blocked-content repulls succeed after ref cleanup but fail with recorded blocked payload requests after pruning. Restored source permits exact-commit deployment; existing app and runtime retain their commits.

notes: Object retention and deletion are observed through public installation operations and fixture-server requests, without inspecting the target's private repository layout.
